dashboardTips: Log the week’s highest-leverage action. If you can’t name one, recalibrate.
Ask “why does this matter” tied to a number before every task.
Checkboxes track effort; checkpoints test capability.
Apply before perfect — the market is part of the feedback loop.
5 focused hours × 6 days beats occasional 12-hour bursts.
Tutorial hell = a second course instead of shipping the build.
One list, one spine per topic. No list-hopping.
dailyLoop: Daily loop: Today → tasks → tick → progress updates → Day 7 review → next day. Weekly: Weekly Plan → Review. Phase end: Assessments → gate. Behind? Recovery Mode.

blueprint.howToUse: Keep the existing 52-week task engine, but follow this page as the career spine. The biggest change is that cloud is no longer a late-stage topic: AWS/networking/IAM/observability begin during the foundation and core-engineering months, then Kubernetes/Terraform/MLOps become deep specialization.
blueprint.rule2: Year 1 = AWS as the primary cloud. Learn GCP/Azure concepts for portability, not full certification tracks.
blueprint.certNote: Current official guidance was re-checked in September 2026. Certification names/status are kept current here; always re-check the exam page immediately before booking.
blueprint.allocationNote: Do not add hours every time a new topic appears. Use the cloud tasks in this roadmap to replace low-value repetition, not to create a 40-hour/week syllabus you cannot sustain.

roadmap.certsNote: Certs are secondary to shipped projects. Only two are scheduled; the rest are sequenced for year 2 with the reason.
roadmap.horizonNote: Everything from the seven sources that belongs to years 2–4. Not scheduled by design: the learning year comes first.
roadmap.depsHelp: Click a node to highlight everything it depends on. Green = the week it starts in is fully done. Scroll sideways.

projectsLead: Mini → intermediate → flagship → capstone. Project tasks also live inside the weekly schedule; this page tracks requirements, milestones and shipping separately.

howItWorks: Daily (10 min): recall yesterday’s main task aloud — auto-added to every day.
Weekly (Day 7): rewrite the week’s key ideas from memory, reimplement two things, re-solve DSA from 3 weeks earlier.
Phase: each gate includes a rapid-recall day and a “fail → revisit” path.
Cumulative: DSA second cold pass over all 175 problems from W30; the 100-problem review list in W50–W52.
revision.masteryLead: Tick an item only when you can do it without notes. A topic is mastered when all items hold.

assessLead: One gate per phase. Move forward when the pass criteria are met — not when the calendar says so. If you fail, the gate tells you exactly what to revisit.
resourcesLead: One primary + one backup per topic. Owned courses are your spine; free resources fill only what they do not reach. Open resource → learn → practice → complete task.
finalLead: Tick only what is true. Anything unticked at W52 gets a date to close it.
recoveryLead: Missed days happen. Do not study more; study the right things, in this order.
coverageLead: Which topics from each original roadmap were incorporated and where they live now. Anything intentionally not scheduled says why.
b75Note: * Blind 75 core. If time is brutally short before an interview, do the * subset first.

tutor.lead: Ready-made prompts that turn Claude into a tutor: it teaches with diagrams and examples, makes you practice, then tests you and reports what to re-study. Placeholders are filled from your current position; edit the topic below and copy.
tutor.workflow: Workflow: open a new Claude chat → paste one prompt → follow its steps → when it says “test me” or you finish, take the test → read the report → tick the mastery checkpoint only if the verdict is “Mastered”. Copy weak items into your Weekly review notes.
tips: One topic per chat. Start a fresh chat for each task so the report is about one thing.
Paste your own code and your own explanation — the value is in Claude correcting your attempt, not producing a perfect one.
Ask for a Mermaid diagram if you want something you can paste into your notes; ask for ASCII if you want something you can redraw from memory.
Never tick a mastery item because the session felt good; tick it when the test report says “Mastered”.
Keep the report: paste “Weak” items into Weekly Plan → Review so Day 7 revision targets them.

sideLead: Self-paced tracks. 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher is the exception: it feeds the weekly recall tasks on Day 7 of W2–W52 (which DO count toward progress) — do its modules in order alongside the main path. The others sit outside the 52-week path, never count toward roadmap progress and must never displace a DSA slot or a flagship milestone.
gateWarning: You are entering {PHASE} but the {PREV} gate is not marked passed. Open Assessments and tick the pass criteria honestly, or follow its “fail → revisit” items first.
dayComplete: Daily checkpoint: can you explain today’s main idea without notes?
